comments.text: The last nine bytes of char_colours (characters $F7-$FF), which this file loads over level 1.1's with the same values. The rest of the level's tiles and character colours ($8009-$86FF) stay as level 1.1 left them.
The addresses of the six map rows, two bytes each: $8715, $87D5, $8895, $8955, $8A15, $8AD5. scroll_column reads them for each new column. The label is the engine's.
map_row_addrs from its second byte: the high byte of row 0's address, and the other rows' (scroll_column reads the high bytes from $870A). The label is the engine's.

Map row 0, the top tile row: one tile number for each map column, 172 columns used of the 192 bytes (the level's length, $AC, at level_end). The row doubles as the column command table: a byte with bit 7 set makes its whole column a command that scroll_column carries out and skips, bit 6 set for the next six sky colours (level_colours_next), clear for the next four band routines (level_band_routines). Command columns: 0 (band routines), 1 (sky colours), 43 (sky colours), 82 (sky colours), 106 (band routines), 114 (band routines), 162 (band routines). The label is the engine's.

Map row 1 of six, the second tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 172 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $00. The label is the engine's.

Map row 2 of six, the third tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 172 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $00. The label is the engine's.

Map row 3 of six, the fourth tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 172 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $4C. The label is the engine's.

Map row 4 of six, the fifth tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 172 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $0F. The label is the engine's.

Map row 5 of six, the bottom tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 172 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $24. The label is the engine's.

The level's length in map columns, $AC (172): scroll_column stops scrolling there ($1216) and wakes objects waiting for the end, and game_frame_music starts the end tune and object_kill counts the end creature's death within three columns of it. The label is the engine's.
The first character Clyde and his shots pass through, $31: player_control, its jump and fall, and shot_hits_wall treat every character below it as wall or floor.

Band colours for $D022, the characters' first multicolour (through $12BD-$12C2): six raster bands for each of six changes, which level_colours_next copies six at a time; the raster routines write a band's value at its top unless bit 7 is set, which leaves the colour from the band above. This level reads changes 0, 1, 2 (the others never read): change 0: dark grey same same same brown same; change 1: dark grey same same same brown same; change 2: dark grey same same same brown same. The label is the engine's.

Band colours for $D023, the second multicolour (through $12C3-$12C8): six raster bands for each of six changes, which level_colours_next copies six at a time; the raster routines write a band's value at its top unless bit 7 is set, which leaves the colour from the band above. This level reads changes 0, 1, 2 (the others never read): change 0: light blue light red grey same light red orange; change 1: light red same grey same light red same; change 2: light red same grey same light red same. The label is the engine's.

Band colours for $D021, the background (through $12C9-$12CE): six raster bands for each of six changes, which level_colours_next copies six at a time; the raster routines write a band's value at its top unless bit 7 is set, which leaves the colour from the band above. This level reads changes 0, 1, 2 (the others never read): change 0: cyan same same same light grey cyan; change 1: cyan same same same light grey cyan; change 2: light blue same same same same same. The label is the engine's.

The band table: four entries per change of band routines, for bands 2-5, each an index into the engine's routine table at $12CF (level_band_routines). This level reads groups 0, 1, 2, 3 (the others never read): 0: 0 1 2 0; 1: 2 0 0 0; 2: 0 1 2 0; 3: 1 0 2 0. The label is the engine's.

The last scroll position of each section: level_section_from_scroll picks the first entry not below the scroll position as the section Clyde restarts in after losing a life: $29 $48 $77 $96 $FF $FF; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

The scroll position (the map column at the right edge) each section restarts from, which get_ready writes to $1273; $FF for the first means from the start: $FF $23 $41 $6F $90 $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

The scroll position at which each section's opening run ends and play begins (stage_start writes it into stage_intro_loop's compare at $1A72): $0C $2F $4C $7B $9B $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

How many map columns the Get Ready screen's landscape strip runs for in each section (get_ready_strip's compare at $3AFE): $27 $3A $57 $83 $A3 $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
The strip's scroll speed for each section (the SBC operand at $3AEA): $02 $03 $04 $05 $06 $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

The x of the Get Ready screen's marker over the landscape strip in each section: raster_ready_marker places three sprites showing block 13 a pixel apart from this x (its LDX operand at $394F); block 13 stays blank until the strip has stopped, when the Get Ready raster code draws a small pattern into it from ready_columns_1: $2D $B0 $B0 $B0 $B0 $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
The marker's y in each section (raster_ready_marker's LDA operand at $395E): $93 $A3 $9B $A3 $A3 $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

The read position in the sky colour tables when a section starts: get_ready copies the six colours from there: $00 $00 $06 $0C $0C $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
Where the sky colour tables are read from after a section starts, for the next colour command: $00 $06 $0C $0C $0C $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

The read position in band_table for each section's start; get_ready reads four entries from it (for a first section's $FC the read runs past band_table into strip_tile_colours and wraps to 0, and the command in map column 0 then sets the bands): $FC $00 $00 $04 $08 $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
Clyde's starting x in each section (into stage_main_setup's LDA at $1A9B): $55 $71 $6D $6D $72 $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
Clyde's starting y in each section (into the LDA at $1AA0): $5D $9D $7D $9D $A2 $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
The low byte of the first spawn record of each section (get_ready into $1FC3): $9000, $9176, $930E, $94C8, $961C, $9000; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
The high byte of each section's first spawn record (into $1FC4): $90 $91 $93 $94 $96 $90; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

The scrolling, in pixels, before each section's first record is read (into the spawn counter $1FC2): $00 $12 $26 $0F $1C $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
print_big's string 1, the stage's name on the Get Ready screen: "STAGE 1.2" and $FF. The label is the engine's.
print_at's string 0, the Get Ready screen's first line, centred in 40 characters: "CREEPY CAVES FOLLOWED BY" and $FF. The label is the engine's.
print_at's string 3, the Get Ready screen's second line: "WATERY FALLS" and $FF. The label is the engine's.

The colours of the Get Ready screen's three potion-creature icons, four sets of three: raster_ready_icons shows the last set first, then steps through the first three every ten frames. green white light blue; green light red white; white light red light blue; green light red light blue. The label is the engine's.
The stage's time limit, three digits: 800. timer_reset copies them to the panel's timer. The label is the engine's.

The level's five hook addresses, copied by level_begin into the engine's calls: $A8BA every frame (level_frame_call), $A305 for Clyde (level_player_call), $A369 for his jump (level_jump_call), $A46C for his animation (level_anim_call) and $A46B in place of firing (level_hook_call). The label is the engine's.
level_hooks' second address, the player routine. The label is the engine's.
level_hooks' third address, the jump routine. The label is the engine's.
level_hooks' fourth address, the animation routine. The label is the engine's.
level_hooks' fifth address, called instead of player_fire. The label is the engine's.
The Get Ready strip's colours, read by raster_ready_strip: orange, brown (the two multicolour registers) and, at $8CF4, light blue for the background. The label is the engine's.
strip_colours' second byte. The label is the engine's.
strip_colours' third byte, the strip's background. The label is the engine's.
The colour of each tile on the Get Ready strip, 96 bytes: get_ready_strip draws each map byte as a single character, the miniature of its tile, in this colour. The label is the engine's.
The Get Ready screen's backdrop character, $42, which get_ready fills the strip's six rows with. The label is the engine's.
The address of the level's tune, $9C7E, played from the start of play when the music option is on (stage_main_setup). The label is the engine's.
tune_addr's high byte. The label is the engine's.
The address of the end tune, $9F00, which game_frame_music starts within three columns of the level's end. The label is the engine's.
end_tune_addr's high byte. The label is the engine's.
The low bytes of the 56 object types' animation scripts; object_set_type and object_spawn read them with anim_hi. The label is the engine's.
The high bytes of the object types' animation scripts. The label is the engine's.
Each object type's animation speed: a new byte of its script every speed + 1 of the object's turns (each object animates every other frame); $7F all but stops it. The label is the engine's.
The low bytes of the 15 colour cycles' lists, chosen by a spawn record's colour byte ($10-$1E) or a death's colour cycle. The label is the engine's.
The high bytes of the colour cycles' lists. The label is the engine's.
Each colour cycle's speed: frames between its colours (obj_cycle_speed). The label is the engine's.
The low bytes of the 32 x movement scripts, named by a spawn record (byte 1, and byte 0's high nibble at death). The label is the engine's.
The high bytes of the x movement scripts. The label is the engine's.
The low bytes of the 32 y movement scripts (record byte 2, and byte 10's high nibble at death). The label is the engine's.
The high bytes of the y movement scripts. The label is the engine's.
Hit points by the low nibble of record byte 9: $FF $00 $01 $02 $03 $04 $05 $09 $10 $27 $45 $63 $2C $AE $C7 $FE ($FF: shots never harm it, they only make it flash). The label is the engine's.

Wake delays by the high nibble of record byte 9: an object with 0 is awake at once; any other value leaves it asleep (obj_awake clear: it neither moves nor animates, and cannot be hit) while objects_scroll counts the value down once a frame, waking it when the count passes zero, except that $FE waits for the level's end, when scroll_column wakes it, and $FF for ever: $00 $01 $02 $03 $04 $05 $61 $62 $63 $64 $65 $40 $20 $FE $80 $FF. The label is the engine's.
Start delays, in frames, by the top two bits of record bytes 1 and 2 together: $00 $01 $10 $0A $38 $30 $A0 $05 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00. The label is the engine's.
Hits needed before an object's hit response runs, by the low nibble of record byte 15: $00 $03 $06 $09 $0C $09 $0F $10 $20 $40 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00 $FF. The label is the engine's.

The low bytes of six message addresses the witch's shop reads from the loaded level ($EB01-$EB65 in the shop's code), high bytes at shop_text_hi: 0 $993C, 1 $8F47, 2 $98FB, 3 $997B, 4 $997B, 5 $98BB. The shop greets Clyde with message 0 when his lives count ($B7BF) is 0, 2 when it is below shop_lives_mark, 1 otherwise; it shows message 3 as its second line and message 5 as the third clue. Nothing reads message 4.
The high bytes of the six shop messages' addresses (see shop_text_lo).
6 (level 1.1 has 3): with a lives count below this (but not 0) the witch's shop greets Clyde with shop_text 2, "YOU BETTER BE MORE CAREFUL"; with this many or more, with shop_text 1.
The x offsets a riding object can take from the object carrying it (ride_parent, by the low nibble of record byte 14): 0 2 4 6 8 10 12 14. The label is the engine's.
The y offsets for a riding object (bits 4-6 of record byte 14): 0 3 6 9 12 15 18 26.
The slot of the level's end creature, 10: killing it within three columns of the level's end starts the stage-complete countdown (object_kill). The label is the engine's.

"USE THE CANNON TO" $FF "STOP THE JACK AND" $FF "SAVE YOUR BUDDY" $FF "CHIP." $00: the first clue the witch's shop sells for torture chamber 1, four lines, each ending in $FF and the message in $00. The shop takes it from this fixed address in every level.
"HI THERE MY CUTE" / "BUNDLE OF FLUFF." / "I'M GLAD YOU'RE" / "DOING WELL." ($FF between lines, $00 at the end): shop_text 1, the witch's greeting when Clyde has shop_lives_mark lives or more.

Animation script of type 55, an invisible object: its script shows only the blank sprite and the collision tests skip type 55 ($37), so it is seen only when it dies, as its death type (type 55 speed 127): frames $0F, then it starts again; named by 4 spawn records.
